question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

My hands are full
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. "To be very busy".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"My hands are full"** means having a lot of responsibilities or being extremely busy. (मेरे हाथ भरे हुए हैं यानी बहुत व्यस्त होना)

 
 
• **Example:** I can't take on any more work right now; my hands are full with the current projects.
 
 
 
• The correct interpretation of this idiom in the context provided is "To be very busy" (बहुत व्यस्त होना).
 
 
• **Example:** With three kids and a full-time job, her hands are always full.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: To dislike someone** (किसी को नापसंद करना): To feel aversion or hatred toward someone.

 
 
• **Example:** She seems to dislike him because of his rude behavior.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: To panic** (घबरा जाना): To feel sudden fear or anxiety.
 
 
• **Example:** When the fire alarm went off, everyone started to panic.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: To go directly towards something** (सीधे किसी चीज़ की ओर जाना): To aim or move straight toward a particular thing.
 
 
• **Example:** He went directly toward the manager to discuss the issue.
